oecd-employment-outlook-2026.title: OECD Employment Outlook 2026 - From Resilience to Risk: Employment and Wages Under Pressure (Ch. 1)
oecd-employment-outlook-2026.excerpt: OECD's flagship employment report finds the youth unemployment gap is real and widening across Australia, Canada, the EU and the US, but attributes it to macro sensitivity rather than LLM diffusion: "the role of LLMs in explaining the unemployment gap of young labour market entrants remains limited, both for those with and without a graduate degree." The ratio of new postings in top- versus bottom-quintile Language Model Exposure occupations "exhibits no break at the end of 2023," when LinkedIn AI-hiring data date the onset of intensive firm LLM use, and the same holds for postings Lightcast flags as junior.

ilo-youth-employment-trends-2026.title: Global Employment Trends for Youth 2026: Back to the Future
ilo-youth-employment-trends-2026.excerpt: "The report estimates that 6.1 per cent of jobs currently held by young people aged 15 to 29 fall in the categories of those most exposed to AI" - 55.8 million of 913.8 million youth jobs globally. Under an illustrative scenario in which a tenth of those jobs disappear outright, "that would translate into 5.6 million employed youth at the global level either facing unemployment, shifting into another job or exiting the labour force." Exposure is concentrated in rich countries: 14.3 per cent of youth jobs in high-income countries and in Northern America, versus 0.9 per cent in low-income countries. ILO cautions that "the degree to which risk translates to job loss is still debatable."

richmond-fed-ai-exposure-job-finding-202.title: Worker Types, AI Exposure and the Recent Decline in Job-Finding Rates (Economic Brief 26-26)
richmond-fed-ai-exposure-job-finding-202.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond (Borovickova, Macaluso)
richmond-fed-ai-exposure-job-finding-202.excerpt: Decomposes the post-2023 decline in job-finding rates by worker type and AI exposure. Entrants are not the margin: "Job-finding rates for new entrants have declined in recent years, but the drop is modest relative to the declines among job losers and job leavers." The decline concentrates instead among strongly attached incumbents in highly AI-exposed occupations, whose job-finding rate fell roughly 13 percentage points against about 2 points for marginally attached workers - a caution that entrant-focused readings of the AI evidence may be misattributing an incumbent phenomenon.

goldman-global-ai-labor-2026.title: Goldman studied where AI is squeezing labor markets. Here's what it found
goldman-global-ai-labor-2026.excerpt: Goldman's first cross-country read on AI and employment. Industries more exposed to AI automation have seen slower job-openings growth since H2 2022, most pronounced in Germany, Australia and the US. Call-center employment is 39% below trend in the US, 33% in Canada and 27% in Germany; software publishing, management consulting and advertising also fell sharply below trend. Across more than 800 occupations, a 10% occupational AI exposure is associated with a 0.1pp drag on annual headcount growth in France, Canada and the US, rising to more than 0.6pp (Australia) and over 0.2pp (US) for entry-level workers. Combining 11 adoption surveys, developed markets sit at roughly 15-20% adoption and emerging markets 10-15%.

goldman-exchanges-briggs-acemoglu-2026.title: How Will AI Impact the Labor Market? (Goldman Sachs Exchanges)
goldman-exchanges-briggs-acemoglu-2026.excerpt: Podcast episode recorded June 2026 with Goldman global economics head Joseph Briggs and MIT's Daron Acemoglu and Neil Thompson. Acemoglu expects "some net job losses, limited, but net job losses within the next five years" at a scale of "less than two to four percent," attributing the ceiling to the absence of reliable off-the-shelf applications built on foundation models, with coding an exception. He sizes the most vulnerable pool, cognitive routine work such as customer service and back office, at eight to nine million US workers, and warns of bigger losses over 10-15 years, with AI-robotics integration the largest wildcard given that physical tasks are about 50% of US work. Briggs puts the current imprint at a 10-15K/month drag on job growth concentrated in tech, consulting and graphic design, and reiterates the 9%/15M ten-year reallocation forecast under a 15% productivity uplift, with any single year's unemployment increase under 1pp. Thompson frames AI as a "rising tide" rather than a "crashing wave."

anthropic-81k-economics-survey-2026.title: What 81,000 people told us about the economics of AI
anthropic-81k-economics-survey-2026.excerpt: Survey of 80,508 Claude.ai users (personal accounts). One fifth voiced concern about economic displacement. Perceived job threat correlated with observed exposure: for every 10pp increase in exposure, perceived threat increased by 1.3pp; top-quartile exposure workers mentioned worry 3x as often as bottom-quartile. Early-career respondents much more likely to express concern than senior workers. Mean productivity rating 5.1/7 ('substantially more productive'); 3% reported negative or neutral impacts, 42% no clear indication. 48% of users mentioning productivity cited scope (new tasks), 40% speed. Management occupations (mostly entrepreneurs) and computer/math groups showed largest gains; scientific and legal professions the mildest. 10% of respondents naming a beneficiary said employers/clients capture the surplus; only 60% of early-career workers said they personally benefited vs 80% of senior professionals. U-shaped relationship between reported speedup and perceived job threat: both those slowed and those sped up most are more anxious.

karger-kuusela-nber-ai-forecasts-2026.title: Forecasting the Economic Effects of AI
karger-kuusela-nber-ai-forecasts-2026.publisher: NBER (Karger, Kuusela, Abaluck, Bryan, Halperin, Jones, Murphy, Trammell, et al.)
karger-kuusela-nber-ai-forecasts-2026.excerpt: NBER Working Paper 35046. Survey of 69 economists, 52 AI industry/policy professionals, 38 superforecasters, and 401 general public on AI's economic effects. Unconditional median economist forecasts: GDP growth 2.5% for 2025–2029, LFPR 61.0% for 2030 (vs 62.6% Jan 2025), 58.3% for 2050. Only 14.0% mean probability assigned to a 'rapid' AI progress scenario by 2030. Conditional on rapid scenario: GDP growth 3.5%, LFPR falling to 55.0% by 2050 (~10M lost jobs attributable to AI), wealth inequality reaching 80.0% held by top 10% by 2050, work hours AI-assisted rising from 3.35% (2024) to 10.1% (2030 unconditional) or 24.2% (2030 rapid). Variance decomposition finds expert disagreement driven primarily by different beliefs about economic effects of highly capable AI systems, not by disagreement about AI capability progress. Economists support retraining (71.8%) over job guarantees (13.7%) or UBI (37.4%); general public supports both.

shah-levy-pro-se-ai-courts-2026.title: Access to Justice in the Age of AI: Evidence from U.S. Federal Courts
shah-levy-pro-se-ai-courts-2026.excerpt: Analysis of 4.5M+ non-prisoner federal civil cases (FY2005-FY2026) and 46M PACER docket entries. Pro se filing share rose from ~11% steady-state (FY2005-FY2022) to 16.8% in FY2025, with pro se case counts nearly doubling (23,210 pre-AI avg → 41,490 in FY2025). Rise concentrated in 'simple' NOS categories (civil rights, consumer credit, foreclosure); absent in patent/securities. Plaintiff-side only — defendant pro se counts fell. Pro se docket entries per court up 158% vs pre-AI mean by 2025Q2; per case up 38% (16.9 → 23.3). Represented entries per case also up 23% (18.2 → 22.5). Case durations and disposition mix unchanged. Pangram AI-text detector applied to 1,600 random complaints (200/yr, 2019-2026): AI-text share rose monotonically from 0.1% pre-AI (1 of 800 false-positive baseline) to 1.0% (2023), 3.5% (2024), 10.5% (2025), 18.0% (early 2026).

gallup-workplace-ai-feb-2026.title: Rising AI Adoption Spurs Workforce Changes
gallup-workplace-ai-feb-2026.excerpt: 28% of employed U.S. adults use AI a few times a week or more; 13% use daily (up from 10% in 2024). 41% of employees report their organization has integrated AI tools. 23% in AI-adopting orgs report workforce reductions vs. 16% in non-adopting. Survey of 23,717 employed U.S. adults, margin of error +/-0.9pp.

galdin-silbert-llm-signaling-2025.title: Making Talk Cheap: Generative AI and Labor Market Signaling
galdin-silbert-llm-signaling-2025.excerpt: LLMs disrupted labor market signaling on Freelancer.com coding jobs (2.7M applications, 61K posts). Employer WTP for 1 SD signal increase fell from $25.67 to $14.85 (42% decline). Counterfactual no-signaling equilibrium: 5% avg wage decline, 1.5% hiring reduction, 4% worker surplus loss, top-quintile hired 19% less, bottom-quintile hired 14% more. 14% of post-LLM apps used AI writing tool.

oecd-ai-sme-adoption-g7-2025.title: AI Adoption by Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
oecd-ai-sme-adoption-g7-2025.publisher: OECD (Calvino, Bianchini, Lane, Montegu, Verger, Ancheva)
oecd-ai-sme-adoption-g7-2025.excerpt: AI adoption in core business functions ranges from 1.9% in Japan to 6.1% in the United States in 2024. cvl-economics-entertainment-ai-2024.excerpt: About 21.4% of film, television, and animation jobs (approximately 118,500 jobs) are likely to be either consolidated, replaced, or eliminated by GenAI in the U.S. by 2026. 75% of survey respondents indicated Gen AI tools had supported the elimination, reduction, or consolidation of jobs in their business division.

oxford-oii-ai-skills-premium-2025.title: Skills or degree? The rise of skill-based hiring for AI and green jobs
oxford-oii-ai-skills-premium-2025.excerpt: AI skills and expertise are highly valued by employers, offering a 23% wage premium, compared to a 13% wage premium for Master's degrees and a 33% premium for PhDs. In science, engineering, and tech jobs, the AI skills premium is 36%. Analysis of over 10 million online job vacancies in the UK between 2018 to 2024.

goldman-briggs-us-labor-2026.excerpt: 6-7% of workers will be displaced during that transition period. In the US, AI can potentially automate tasks that account for 25% of all work hours. Goldman Sachs Research expects to see a 0.6 percentage point increase in the unemployment rate over a decade.

freund-mann-job-transformation-2026.title: Job Transformation, Specialization, and the Labor Market Effects of AI
freund-mann-job-transformation-2026.excerpt: average individual wages are roughly unchanged for incumbents of occupations with no AI exposure, rise by around 4% at moderate exposure, and drop by as much as 35% for workers in the most exposed occupations

coworkingcafe-ai-jobs-metros-2026.title: The New Map of AI Work: San Jose Builds It & New York Scales It

For comparison, in Dallas–Fort Worth, TX, $128,000 salaries stretch further with costs just 3% above average.

imas-demand-collapse-ai-2026.title: Can advanced AI lead to negative economic growth?
imas-demand-collapse-ai-2026.excerpt: automation can depress demand and push AI-driven growth toward the lower end of current forecasts. [...] the conditions needed for growth to actually turn negative are likely too unrealistic to hold in practice

imas-shukla-oring-exposure-2026.title: How Will AI-driven Automation Actually Affect Jobs?
imas-shukla-oring-exposure-2026.publisher: Substack (Alex Imas, Soumitra Shukla — U of Chicago Booth)
imas-shukla-oring-exposure-2026.excerpt: Two jobs with identical exposure scores can have completely opposite displacement risks depending on whether their tasks are complements, whether demand for their output is elastic or inelastic, and the incentives of the firm to invest in automation. The workers at greatest risk are not necessarily those with the highest average exposure, but those whose jobs are built around a small number of core tasks that AI can automate.

gans-goldfarb-oring-automation-2026.title: O-Ring Automation
gans-goldfarb-oring-automation-2026.excerpt: Widely-used exposure indices, which aggregate task-level automation risk using linear formulas, will overstate displacement when tasks are complements. Labour income can rise under partial automation because automation scales the value of remaining bottleneck tasks.

lodefalk-age-gradient-hiring-2026.title: Same Storm, Different Boats: Generative AI and the Age Gradient in Hiring
lodefalk-age-gradient-hiring-2026.publisher: RATIO Institute / Örebro University (Lodefalk, Löthman, Koch, Engberg)

manning-aguirre-adaptive-2026.title: How Adaptable Are American Workers to AI-Induced Job Displacement?
manning-aguirre-adaptive-2026.excerpt: 6.1 million workers in AI-exposed roles lack adaptive capacity; 86% are women. Vulnerability concentrated in college towns and state capitals in Mountain West and Midwest.

bessen-automatic-reaction-2025.title: Automatic Reaction — What Happens to Workers at Firms that Automate?
bessen-automatic-reaction-2025.publisher: Review of Economics and Statistics (Bessen, Goos, Salomons, van den Berge)
bessen-automatic-reaction-2025.excerpt: Tenured workers cumulatively lose about 3,800 Euros in wage and salary earnings over five years on average (about 9% of one year's income). Only 0.7% of all workers leave their employers each year due to automation, far below mass layoff rates.

bessen-ai-jobs-demand-2018.title: AI and Jobs: The Role of Demand
bessen-ai-jobs-demand-2018.excerpt: If demand is sufficiently elastic and AI does not completely replace humans, then technical change will create jobs rather than destroy them. Manufacturing employment followed an inverted-U driven by demand elasticity.

hunt-cockburn-bessen-ai-distance-adoptio.title: Is Distance from Innovation a Barrier to the Adoption of Artificial Intelligence?
hunt-cockburn-bessen-ai-distance-adoptio.excerpt: A commuting zone which is an additional 200 km from the closest AI hotspot has 17% lower growth in AI jobs' share of vacancies. 20% of the effect is explained by state borders.

wapo-ai-jobs-adapt-2026.title: See which jobs are most threatened by AI, and who may be able to adapt
wapo-ai-jobs-adapt-2026.excerpt: Two points of general agreement stand out: There's no measurable evidence so far that AI is putting Americans as a whole out of work, economists say. And while the victims of past workplace automation were mostly factory and trade workers, it's white collar jobs that are first in line for AI shake-ups today.

bessen-automation-employment-demand-2019.title: Automation and jobs: when technology boosts employment
bessen-automation-employment-demand-2019.excerpt: The main impact of automation in the near future may be to cause a major reallocation of jobs, even if it does not permanently eliminate large numbers of jobs. During the 19th century, technologies had automated 98% of the labour required to weave a yard of cloth. Yet, the number of weaving jobs actually increased for decades over this period.

revelio-labs-wage-divide-2025.title: The Wage Divide is Widening Again and AI May Be to Blame
revelio-labs-wage-divide-2025.excerpt: Since January 2023, salaries at the top quartile of the wage distribution have grown by more than 30%. Over the same period, salaries at the bottom quartile have risen by only around 10%.

cognizant-new-work-2026.title: New Work, New World 2026: How AI is Reshaping Work
cognizant-new-work-2026.excerpt: Education task exposure jumped from 11% to 49% — a 4.5x increase driven by multimodal AI, advanced reasoning, and agentic systems. Based on reassessment of 18,000 tasks across 1,000 O*NET occupations.

cui-microsoft-copilot-2025.title: The Effects of Generative AI on Computing Workers' Productivity

dallas-fed-entry-level-2026.title: Young workers' employment drops in occupations with high AI exposure

deloitte-ai-state-2024.title: State of Generative AI in the Enterprise Q3 2024

educause-ai-higher-ed-2026.title: The Impact of AI on Work in Higher Education

egon-zehnder-cfo-ai-2025.title: AI Revolution: CFOs Forecast a Transformation in Finance Teams

eloundou-openai-2024.title: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of LLMs

epi-wages-2025.title: Unbalanced labor market power is what makes technology — including AI — threatening to workers

experian-health-claims-2025.title: State of Claims 2025: AI and Claims Processing
experian-health-claims-2025.excerpt: 67% of providers believe AI can improve claims processing, but only 14% have implemented AI tools. Among adopters, 69% report reduced denials. Survey of 250 providers.

glassdoor-ai-salaries-2025.title: Conversation starter: are AI jobs booming or overhyped?
glassdoor-ai-salaries-2025.excerpt: AI jobs pay more than similar jobs that do not focus on AI, with a typical premium of 25%. The share of AI jobs among new job listings increased 123% from 2023 to 2024.

goldman-300m.excerpt: Roughly two-thirds of current jobs are exposed to some degree of AI automation; generative AI could substitute up to one-fourth of current work.

goldman-ai-workforce-2025.excerpt: Young tech workers (20-30) unemployment risen ~3pp since start of 2025; tech employment share fallen below pre-pandemic trend.

goldman-mei-ai-labor-2026.title: AI and the US Labor Market: Current Impact and Outlook
goldman-mei-ai-labor-2026.excerpt: AI's labor market impact still small — only 5-10K/month drag on net job growth. Only 2½% of jobs exposed to automation today. google-10k-2024.title: Alphabet Inc. 2024 10-K — Workforce & AI Automation Disclosures
google-10k-2024.excerpt: Alphabet disclosed ongoing workforce restructuring, noting AI tools have reduced need for certain engineering and support roles while increasing demand for AI/ML specialists.

hartley-genai-labor-2026.title: The Labor Market Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence
hartley-genai-labor-2026.publisher: Stanford / World Bank (Hartley, Jolevski, Melo, Moore)
hartley-genai-labor-2026.excerpt: 35.9% of US workers used generative AI by December 2025; small positive wage effects, no significant decline in job openings.

hbs-chen-srinivasan-displacement-complem.title: Displacement or Complementarity? The Labor Market Impact of Generative AI
hbs-chen-srinivasan-displacement-complem.excerpt: Using O*NET and LightCast job postings data (2019-June 2024), the study found a 24% decrease in generative AI-exposed skills per firm per quarter for automation-prone occupations, while augmentation-prone occupations saw a 15% increase. Demonstrates the dual displacement/complementarity impact of generative AI.

harvard-workforce-almanac-2025.title: The Workforce Almanac: A System-Level View of U.S. Workforce Training Providers (v2.0)
harvard-workforce-almanac-2025.publisher: Harvard Kennedy School Project on Workforce (Fuller, Gable, Forshaw, Hale, Gazzaneo, Simsek)
harvard-workforce-almanac-2025.excerpt: A public-use directory of 20,211 short-term US workforce training providers, up from roughly 17,000 at the November 2023 launch, built by combining IPEDS, TrainingProviderResults.gov, IRS Form 990 series, and RAPIDS into one deduplicated file. Scope is post-high-school training lasting under two years. Providers sort into job training nonprofits (7,408, 37%), WIOA-eligible providers (29%), sub-baccalaureate higher education institutions (3,648, 18%), and Registered Apprenticeship sponsors (3,347, 16%). The authors note it still underestimates the true provider count, so the figures are a floor. Held in the library rather than plotted: it carries no AI attribution and no employment, wage, or training-outcome measure, so it maps to no prediction graph. Its use is as a supply-side denominator for reskilling capacity against the displacement estimates elsewhere in the corpus. Funded by Strada Education Foundation and WorkRise.

harvard-edtech-2024.title: Professor tailored AI tutor to physics course. Engagement doubled.
harvard-edtech-2024.excerpt: Learning gains for students in the AI-tutored group were about double those for the in-class group. Students using the AI tutor reported significantly more engagement and motivation to learn.

hbr-ai-potential-layoffs-2026.title: Companies Are Laying Off Workers Because of AI's Potential, Not Its Performance
hbr-ai-potential-layoffs-2026.excerpt: 95% of generative AI projects have failed to deliver measurable returns (citing MIT). PwC: 56% of CEOs said AI failed to boost revenue or lower costs. Layoffs are anticipatory, not performance-driven.

hbr-ai-workslop-2025.title: AI-Generated 'Workslop' Is Destroying Productivity

hosseini-brookings-freelancer-2025.excerpt: High-skill freelancers disproportionately affected by AI — top performers were impacted most, contradicting conventional wisdom that expertise insulates workers.

huang-cs-2024.title: Generative AI and Customer Service: Evidence from Customer Support Interactions

humlum-vestergaard-chatgpt-adoption-2025.excerpt: Half of workers in AI-exposed occupations have used ChatGPT; adoption unequal — women 16pp less likely, employer restrictions hinder broader use.

morgan-stanley-workforce-cut-2026.title: Morgan Stanley Signals New Era of Efficiency with 3% Workforce Reduction Amidst Record Profits
morgan-stanley-workforce-cut-2026.excerpt: 3% workforce reduction amidst record profits; investment banking revenue up 47%.

acemoglu-restrepo-robots-jpe-2020.title: Robots and Jobs: Evidence from US Labor Markets
acemoglu-restrepo-robots-jpe-2020.excerpt: One more robot per thousand workers reduces the employment-to-population ratio by 0.2 percentage points and wages by 0.42%. Between 1990 and 2007, the increase in robots reduced employment by about 400,000 workers.

ifr-world-robotics-2025.title: World Robotics 2025 — Industrial Robots
ifr-world-robotics-2025.excerpt: 542,000 industrial robots installed in 2024 — more than double the number 10 years ago. 4,664,000 robots operational worldwide. US installations at 34,200 units. Global market value $16.5 billion.

wef-future-of-jobs-2025.title: Future of Jobs Report 2025
wef-future-of-jobs-2025.excerpt: Robotics and automation expected to drive business transformation for 58% of employers. Robots and automation forecast to displace 5 million more jobs than they create. 92 million jobs displaced, 170 million created, net +78 million by 2030.

mckinsey-agents-robots-2025.title: Agents, Robots, and Us: Skill Partnerships in the Age of AI
mckinsey-agents-robots-2025.excerpt: 57% of US work hours are technically automatable. Physical tasks comprise 50%+ of hours for 40% of the US workforce. Robot unit costs ($150-500K) must fall to $20-50K for mass physical automation adoption. At least 14% of employees globally may need career changes by 2030.

oecd-automation-risk-2024.title: The Risk of Automation for Jobs in OECD Countries
oecd-automation-risk-2024.excerpt: 14% of jobs across OECD countries are at high risk of automation. An additional 32% may be significantly changed but not eliminated. 27% of jobs at high risk when including all automation technologies including AI.

bls-employment-projections-2026.title: Industry and Occupational Employment Projections Overview 2024-34
bls-employment-projections-2026.excerpt: Retail trade projected to decline 1.2% as automation and e-commerce reduce sales occupations. Mining/extraction declining 1.6% driven by robotics and drones. Total employment projected to grow 3.1% (2024-34), much slower than prior decade.

bls-ai-exposure-categories-2026.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) exposure categories
bls-ai-exposure-categories-2026.excerpt: BLS combined five external data sources to create a four-category classification of relative AI exposure for every detailed occupation for which projections are produced. Across 4,155 possible occupation-source combinations for the detailed occupations for which BLS publishes projections data (831 occupations times 5 sources), 3,944 were observed and 211 were imputed, affecting 75 occupations. Exposure does not imply job loss, productivity gains, automation probability, or wage effects.

amazon-robotics-2025.title: Amazon Fulfillment Center Robotics Deployment
amazon-robotics-2025.excerpt: Amazon deployed roughly 800,000 mobile robots across its fulfillment centers by 2024, making it the largest private deployer of mobile robots globally.

goldman-physical-ai-2025.title: The Dawn of Humanoid Robots and Physical AI
goldman-physical-ai-2025.excerpt: Physically demanding or outdoor work unlikely to be affected by current AI. Projects 50,000-100,000 humanoid robot shipments in 2026. Unit economics expected to reach $15,000-$20,000 per robot.

shrm-automation-risk-2025.title: Jobs at High Risk of Automation in the US
shrm-automation-risk-2025.excerpt: 15% of US jobs — about 23 million total — are at high risk of displacement due to automation, concentrated in manufacturing, transportation, and food preparation.

bls-manufacturing-decline-2025.title: US Manufacturing Employment Declines as Automation Ramps Up
bls-manufacturing-decline-2025.excerpt: US manufacturing lost 78,000 jobs over the past year with 12,000 cuts in August alone. Manufacturing employment at lowest level since onset of COVID-19 pandemic.

stl-fed-robots-employment-2024.title: How Robots Affect Employment
stl-fed-robots-employment-2024.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
stl-fed-robots-employment-2024.excerpt: Robots have a mixed effect: replacing jobs that relatively high-wage manufacturing employees used to perform, while also making firms more efficient and productive. One robot per thousand workers replaced about six workers.

piie-kolko-ai-labor-first-inning-2026.title: Research on AI and the labor market is still in the first inning
piie-kolko-ai-labor-first-inning-2026.publisher: Peterson Institute for International Economics (Jed Kolko)
piie-kolko-ai-labor-first-inning-2026.excerpt: The evidence on how AI is affecting the labor market today is inconclusive, and claims about harmful impacts on particular groups of workers are premature. Initial evidence suggests that transitional disruption from AI to date is not outpacing recent technological changes.

anthropic-shen-ai-skill-formation-2026.title: How AI Impacts Skill Formation
anthropic-shen-ai-skill-formation-2026.excerpt: AI use impairs conceptual understanding, code reading, and debugging abilities. The AI group averaged 50% on the quiz, compared to 67% in the hand-coding group.

oecd-ai-skills-gap-2025.title: Bridging the AI Skills Gap: Is Training Keeping Up?
oecd-ai-skills-gap-2025.excerpt: With one in three job vacancies having high AI exposure, a significant share of jobs in OECD economies are influenced by the rise of AI.

nhh-carvajal-ai-gender-gap-2024.title: Will Artificial Intelligence Get in the Way of Achieving Gender Equality?
nhh-carvajal-ai-gender-gap-2024.publisher: NHH Norwegian School of Economics (Carvajal, Franco, Isaksson)
nhh-carvajal-ai-gender-gap-2024.excerpt: Among 595 business school students in Norway, male students were 25 percent more likely to be high AI users, and the gap was widest among the highest-performing women.

chen-stratton-ai-in-firm-2026.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Firm
chen-stratton-ai-in-firm-2026.excerpt: AI adoption led to moderate productivity increases — an 8.5 percent increase in coding activity and 8.7 percent faster task completion — with no measurable quality declines. These productivity gains did not translate into increased output, changes in task composition, or effects on employment.

nber-delfino-unwilling-reskill-2026.title: Unwilling to Reskill? Experimental Evidence from Real-World Jobseekers
nber-delfino-unwilling-reskill-2026.excerpt: Perceived 'identity fit' — whether a new skill feels compatible with a person's sense of self — dominated re-skilling decisions, often outweighing beliefs about wages or employer demand.

bloomberry-180m-creative-postings-2025.title: I analyzed 180M jobs to see what jobs AI is actually replacing today
bloomberry-180m-creative-postings-2025.excerpt: Computer graphic artist postings down 33% in 2025, photographers and writers down 28%, journalists down 22%, against an 8% overall market decline. Analysis of 180M global job postings from company websites using 650 normalized job titles.

mckinsey-agents-robots-us-2025.title: Agents, robots, and us: Skill partnerships in the age of AI
mckinsey-agents-robots-us-2025.publisher: McKinsey Global Institute (Yee, Madgavkar, Smit et al.)
mckinsey-agents-robots-us-2025.excerpt: Currently demonstrated technologies could automate activities accounting for about 57 percent of US work hours today. AI agents could perform tasks occupying 44 percent of US work hours, while robots could handle another 13 percent. Roles with the highest potential for automation make up about 40 percent of total jobs.

nber-wang-wong-tech-unemployment-2025.title: Artificial Intelligence and Technological Unemployment
nber-wang-wong-tech-unemployment-2025.publisher: NBER / Richmond Fed (Ping Wang, Tsz-Nga Wong)
nber-wang-wong-tech-unemployment-2025.excerpt: Calibrated to U.S. data, the model predicts more than threefold improvements in productivity in the some-AI steady state, alongside a long-run employment loss of 23%, with half this loss occurring over the initial five-year transition.

upwork-fy2025-earnings.title: Upwork Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Financial Results
upwork-fy2025-earnings.excerpt: Revenue grew 2% year over year to $787.8 million for full year 2025. GSV per active client was $5,129 in Q4 2025, an increase of 7% year over year. AI-related skills grew by 109% year over year. Active clients were 785,000 as of December 31, 2025.

fiverr-fy2025-earnings.title: Fiverr Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Results
fiverr-fy2025-earnings.publisher: Fiverr International Ltd. (SEC Filing / Press Release)
fiverr-fy2025-earnings.excerpt: Full-year 2025 revenue of $430.9M, up 10.1% YoY. Active buyers down 13.6% in 2025. Spend per buyer reached $342, rising 13% YoY. Writing, translation, and simple programming categories declining ~20% due to AI substitution. High-value projects over $1,000 grew 23%. 2026 revenue guidance: $380M-$420M, a decline of 3-12% YoY.

apoorv03-consumer-ai-usage-2026.title: The State of Consumer AI. Part 1 - Usage
apoorv03-consumer-ai-usage-2026.excerpt: Today, AI apps have crossed 1 billion weekly active users and ChatGPT alone accounts for 900M of that.

oecd-health-ai-workforce-2024.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Health Workforce: Perspectives from Medical Associations
oecd-health-ai-workforce-2024.excerpt: Up to 30% of all administrative tasks performed by physicians, dentists, pharmacists, and specialists can be automated by 2030.

caqh-index-2025.title: 2025 CAQH Index Shows U.S. Healthcare Avoided $258 Billion and Accelerated Automation
caqh-index-2025.excerpt: U.S. healthcare avoided $258B in admin costs. 50%+ of health plans and 25% of provider organizations use AI tools in admin workflows.

pew-ai-experts-predictions-2025.title: Predictions for AI's Next 20 Years by the US Public and AI Experts
pew-ai-experts-predictions-2025.excerpt: 31% of AI experts predict AI will lead to fewer teacher jobs in 20 years. Survey of 1,013 AI experts and 5,410 US adults.

oks-atm-iphone-displacement-2026.title: Why the ATM didn't kill bank teller jobs, but the iPhone did
oks-atm-iphone-displacement-2026.excerpt: I'm skeptical that simply slotting AI into human-shaped jobs will have the results people seem to expect... as long as we are in that regime, I expect disappointing productivity gains and relatively little real displacement.

bizjournals-ai-layoffs-divide-2026.title: AI-fueled layoffs are rising, but a great divide is emerging
bizjournals-ai-layoffs-divide-2026.excerpt: 89% of the respondents said they have no plans to cut staff or lay off workers because of AI. Just 3% said they have already cut staff, while 7% said they have plans to reduce their workforce within the next year.

google-amie-clinical-feasibility-2026.title: A prospective clinical feasibility study of a conversational diagnostic AI in an ambulatory primary care clinic
google-amie-clinical-feasibility-2026.publisher: Google Research / Google DeepMind / Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center
google-amie-clinical-feasibility-2026.excerpt: AMIE's differential diagnosis included the final diagnosis in 90% of cases, with 75% top-3 accuracy. Blinded assessment suggested similar overall DDx and Mx plan quality between AMIE and PCPs. Human safety supervisors did not need to intervene to stop any consultations.

esb-dutch-youth-genai-employment-2026.title: Dalende werkgelegenheid onder Nederlandse jongeren die concurreren met GenAI
esb-dutch-youth-genai-employment-2026.excerpt: In het derde kwartaal van 2025 werkten ruim dertien procent minder jongeren in de meest vatbare beroepsgroepen dan in het vierde kwartaal van 2022, terwijl de werkgelegenheid in andere beroepsgroepen juist drie procent steeg.

stevens-freelance-marketplace-2026.title: Freelance Marketplace Spend Collapse After ChatGPT
stevens-freelance-marketplace-2026.excerpt: Freelance marketplace spend collapsed from 0.66% to 0.14% of GDP after ChatGPT launch.

kim-jin-lee-pixiv-illustrators-2026.title: AI Impact on Pixiv Illustrators
kim-jin-lee-pixiv-illustrators-2026.excerpt: Pixiv illustrator uploads down 10.1% post-AI; commercial creators saw -14.3% decline.

boke-gallemore-glaeser-accounting-ai-202.title: Artificial Intelligence and White-Collar Work: Evidence from the Accounting Profession
boke-gallemore-glaeser-accounting-ai-202.publisher: SSRN (Boke, De la Parra, Gallemore, Glaeser)
boke-gallemore-glaeser-accounting-ai-202.excerpt: AI investment reduces accounting hiring but not work quality. 10 additional AI accounting roles associated with 49 fewer accounting-skill postings.

maasoum-lichtinger-seniority-2025.title: GenAI and Seniority Composition
maasoum-lichtinger-seniority-2025.excerpt: GenAI adopters cut junior hiring 22%; seniority composition shifts toward more experienced workers.

dillon-shifting-work-patterns-2025.title: Shifting Work Patterns with Generative AI
dillon-shifting-work-patterns-2025.publisher: NBER / AER: Insights (Dillon, Jaffe, Immorlica, Stanton)
dillon-shifting-work-patterns-2025.excerpt: In a field experiment across 66 firms and 7,137 knowledge workers, the 80% of treated workers who used the AI tool spent two fewer hours on email each week. We do not detect shifts in the quantity or composition of workers' tasks.

chatterji-chatgpt-usage-2025.title: How People Use ChatGPT
chatterji-chatgpt-usage-2025.publisher: NBER (Chatterji, Cunningham, Deming, Hitzig, Ong, Shan, Wadman)
chatterji-chatgpt-usage-2025.excerpt: By July 2025, 18 billion messages were being sent each week by 700 million users. 81% of work-related messages involve obtaining information or making decisions, not task automation.

dellacqua-cybernetic-teammate-2025.title: The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise
dellacqua-cybernetic-teammate-2025.excerpt: In a pre-registered RCT with 776 P&G professionals, individuals with AI matched teams without AI (+0.37 SD improvement). AI broke professional silos.

choi-xie-human-ai-accounting-2025.title: Human + AI in Accounting: Early Evidence from the Field
choi-xie-human-ai-accounting-2025.excerpt: AI-adopting accountants see 55% increase in weekly client support, 8.5% of time reallocated from data entry to high-value tasks, 12% increase in ledger granularity, and 7.5-day reduction in monthly close time.

fouarge-montizaan-zwick-ai-risk-2024.title: Is my job at risk? Workers' perceived risk of AI
fouarge-montizaan-zwick-ai-risk-2024.excerpt: Financial sector workers perceive highest threat from AI. Age, tenure, and education moderate perceived AI displacement risk.

cao-cheng-gu-jiang-chatgpt-analysts-2025.title: ChatGPT and Financial Analysts
cao-cheng-gu-jiang-chatgpt-analysts-2025.excerpt: ChatGPT cuts analyst report length by 8.9% and reduces quality by 17%. Greater AI reliance is associated with worse earnings forecasts.

bonfiglioli-ai-epop-2025.title: AI Adoption and Employment-to-Population Ratio
bonfiglioli-ai-epop-2025.excerpt: AI adoption associated with -0.6 percentage point decline in employment-to-population ratio.

abrahams-levy-metros-ai-2025.title: Geographic Vulnerability to AI Displacement
abrahams-levy-metros-ai-2025.excerpt: High-education, high-cost metros are most vulnerable to AI displacement.

bao-lou-sun-genai-entrepreneurship-2025.title: Generative AI and Entrepreneurial Entry
bao-lou-sun-genai-entrepreneurship-2025.excerpt: GenAI access leads to increased incorporated entrepreneurship for individuals with higher GenAI exposure -- effect specific to STEM population. Mechanism tests support the augmentation channel.

aldasoro-bis-eu-firms-ai-2026.title: AI Adoption and Employment in EU Firms
aldasoro-bis-eu-firms-ai-2026.excerpt: EU firms see +4% productivity from AI adoption; no employment decline detected.

daniotti-ai-code-diffusion-2025.title: Who is using AI to code? Global diffusion and impact of generative AI
daniotti-ai-code-diffusion-2025.excerpt: AI-assisted coding jumped from around 5% in 2022 to nearly 30% in the last quarter of 2024. Quarterly output has increased by 3.6%. Experienced programmers benefit more; beginners hardly benefit at all.

sarkar-cursor-agents-2025.title: AI Agents, Productivity, and Higher-Order Thinking: Early Evidence From Software Development
sarkar-cursor-agents-2025.publisher: SSRN (Suproteem K. Sarkar, University of Chicago)
sarkar-cursor-agents-2025.excerpt: Software output increased by 39% after the AI agent became the platform's default code generation mode. Quality did not deteriorate. Senior developers benefit most from agents; junior developers benefit most from autocomplete.

baird-linkedin-copilot-2024.title: GitHub Copilot and Developer Productivity
baird-linkedin-copilot-2024.excerpt: GitHub Copilot users show increased code output but no evidence of displacement in hiring patterns.

hoffmann-ai-code-security-2024.title: AI-Generated Code Security Risks
hoffmann-ai-code-security-2024.excerpt: AI-generated code has 41% more vulnerabilities than human-written code. Developers overestimate the security of AI-generated code.

anthropic-economic-index-softdev-2025.title: Anthropic Economic Index: Software Development
anthropic-economic-index-softdev-2025.excerpt: 37% of software development tasks show AI involvement. Writing code is 18% of actual AI usage in software development; most use is for understanding, debugging, and reviewing code.

marguerit-augmenting-automating-2025.title: Augmenting or Automating Labor?
marguerit-augmenting-automating-2025.excerpt: Augmentation AI fosters new work and raises wages for high-skilled occupations.

maasoum-lichtinger-entry-barriers-2026.title: Generative AI and Occupational Entry Barriers: The Labor-Supply Channel of Technological Change
maasoum-lichtinger-entry-barriers-2026.excerpt: GenAI reshapes wage inequality through a productivity-scarcity race: productivity gains widen wage disparities while reduced entry barriers compress them. Net effect is a modest increase in inequality.

pwc-ai-jobs-barometer-2025.title: PwC Global AI Jobs Barometer 2025
pwc-ai-jobs-barometer-2025.excerpt: AI-skilled workers command a 56% wage premium, up from 25% in prior year. AI roles median compensation at $157K vs. $49,500 all-occupation median.

jiang-extended-workday-2025.title: AI and the Extended Workday
jiang-extended-workday-2025.excerpt: When someone transitions to a job with high exposure to AI, they work 3.5 hours longer per week. Productivity gains captured by firms, not wages.

klump-robots-wages-meta-2025.title: Robots and Wages: A Meta-Analysis
klump-robots-wages-meta-2025.publisher: Structural Change and Economic Dynamics (Klump, Schneider, Jurkat)
klump-robots-wages-meta-2025.excerpt: The overall effect of industrial robots on wages is close to zero and insignificant. 53 papers, 2,143 estimations.

merali-scaling-laws-productivity-2025.title: Scaling Laws for Economic Productivity
merali-scaling-laws-productivity-2025.excerpt: Each year of AI model progress reduced task time by 8%. Access to any AI model increased Earnings Per Minute by 81.3%. Continued scaling could boost US productivity by ~20% over the next decade.

tamkin-mccrory-claude-productivity-2025.title: Estimating AI Productivity Gains from Claude Conversations
tamkin-mccrory-claude-productivity-2025.excerpt: Claude speeds up individual tasks by about 80%. Extrapolating suggests 1.8% annual US productivity growth over the next decade.

dubal-negron-surveillance-pay-2025.title: How AI uncouples hard work from fair wages through surveillance pay
dubal-negron-surveillance-pay-2025.publisher: Washington Center for Equitable Growth (Dubal, Negron)
dubal-negron-surveillance-pay-2025.excerpt: Audit of 500 AI vendors finds surveillance pay spreading across healthcare, customer service, and logistics.

fang-genai-retail-productivity-2025.title: Generative AI and Firm Productivity: Field Experiments in Online Retail
fang-genai-retail-productivity-2025.excerpt: Large-scale field experiments find treatment effects 0-16.3% on sales, mapping directly into TFP improvements.

bis-bulletin86-genai-households-2024.title: Survey evidence on gen AI and households: job prospects amid trust concerns
bis-bulletin86-genai-households-2024.excerpt: Almost half of US households use generative artificial intelligence tools. Average expected probability of higher productivity: 30%; of job loss: 13%.

yougov-ai-skepticism-2025.title: Americans are increasingly skeptical about AI's effects
yougov-ai-skepticism-2025.excerpt: 56% of Americans use AI tools; 28% weekly. Skepticism about AI's effects increased 8 percentage points year over year.

microsoft-wti-2025.title: 2025 Work Trend Index
microsoft-wti-2025.excerpt: 75% of knowledge workers use AI at work. 78% bring their own AI tools. Survey of 31,000 workers across 31 countries.

alikhani-brookings-genai-adoption-2025.title: GenAI Adoption Patterns
alikhani-brookings-genai-adoption-2025.excerpt: About 20% use AI professionally; 57% personal use. Adoption varies significantly by education and income.

stephany-duszynski-gender-gap-2026.title: Gender Gap in AI Adoption
stephany-duszynski-gender-gap-2026.excerpt: Gender gap in AI adoption: women adopt less; 5.3 percentage point gap in UK data.

uk-gds-copilot-2025.title: GitHub Copilot in UK Civil Service
uk-gds-copilot-2025.excerpt: GitHub Copilot saves 26 minutes per day across 20,000 UK civil servants.

carioli-zew-skills-shortage-ai-2024.title: Evidence on the Adoption of Artificial Intelligence: The Role of Skills Shortage
carioli-zew-skills-shortage-ai-2024.excerpt: Skills shortage has a positive and significant effect on AI adoption breadth and application areas (German Mannheim Innovation Panel).

wharton-korst-enterprise-ai-2024.title: Enterprise AI Adoption Survey
wharton-korst-enterprise-ai-2024.excerpt: 72% of enterprise leaders use AI weekly; 62% of companies actively use AI (n=800).

ny-fed-ai-adoption-2025.title: AI Adoption in US Firms
ny-fed-ai-adoption-2025.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York (Abel et al.)
ny-fed-ai-adoption-2025.excerpt: Over 50% of information/finance firms use AI; few report layoffs from AI adoption.

menkhoff-cesinfo-ai-adoption-rct-2025.title: Information Nudges and AI Adoption
menkhoff-cesinfo-ai-adoption-rct-2025.excerpt: RCT shows information about AI productivity gains increases adoption among German firms.

auer-bis-skills-exposure-2024.title: Skills Exposure to AI
auer-bis-skills-exposure-2024.excerpt: 17-36% of worker skills exposed at moderate-to-high AI capability level.

brynjolfsson-shao-task-automation-2025.title: Worker Preferences for Task Automation
brynjolfsson-shao-task-automation-2025.excerpt: Workers want 46% of their tasks automated; preferences vary by task type and worker characteristics.

morgan-stanley-ai-survey-2026.title: AI's Impact Accelerates: AlphaWise Survey of 935 Executives
morgan-stanley-ai-survey-2026.excerpt: Survey respondents said that AI adoption had led to elimination of 11% of jobs and an additional 12% were left unfilled. This is partially offset by 18% new hires, resulting in a 4% net job loss globally.

deutsche-bank-ai-predictions-2026.title: What AI Says About AI Eating Itself and the World
deutsche-bank-ai-predictions-2026.excerpt: Customer service could see as much as 75% of interactions automated by 2026. AI-driven platforms could deliver primary investment advice to nearly 80% of retail investors by 2027. Over 85% of software developers now use AI coding assistants, delivering productivity gains of up to 60%.

trinity-health-rcm-layoffs-2026.title: Trinity Health to lay off 10.5% of revenue cycle headcount
trinity-health-rcm-layoffs-2026.excerpt: Trinity Health is laying off 10.5% of its revenue cycle management staff across 15 states and 92 hospitals. Non-patient-facing revenue cycle functions will be transitioned to an external partner.

yale-budgetlab-exposure-agreement-2026.title: Labor Market AI Exposure: What Do We Know?
yale-budgetlab-exposure-agreement-2026.publisher: The Budget Lab at Yale (Gimbel, Kendall, Kulsakdinun)
yale-budgetlab-exposure-agreement-2026.excerpt: AI exposure metrics broadly agree with each other, but that they disagree with each other more on highly exposed occupations. The key point of disagreement between different AI exposure metrics is in the magnitude of exposure, not whether an occupation is exposed.

yale-budgetlab-occupation-exposure-2026.title: Labor Market AI Exposure: What Do We Know? (Data Repository)
yale-budgetlab-occupation-exposure-2026.publisher: The Budget Lab at Yale (Gimbel, Kendall, Kulsakdinun)
yale-budgetlab-occupation-exposure-2026.excerpt: GPT-scored AI exposure for 342 BLS occupations on a 0-10 scale, validated against 6 academic metrics (Pearson 0.878 with Yale PCA, 0.885 with OpenAI). Employment-weighted industry exposure scores for 186 4-digit NAICS industries.

fed-atl-duke-cfo-ai-productivity-2026.title: Artificial Intelligence, Productivity, and the Workforce: Evidence from Corporate Executives
fed-atl-duke-cfo-ai-productivity-2026.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta / Duke University (Baslandze et al.)
fed-atl-duke-cfo-ai-productivity-2026.excerpt: Survey of ~750 CFOs finds AI adoption widespread (58.5% in 2025, 85.4% expected 2026). Implied revenue-based labor productivity gains of 0.6% in 2025, 1.8% expected 2026, with largest gains in finance (>2%). Aggregate employment decline <0.4% in 2026 (~502K workers). Routine clerical roles declining; skilled-technical rising. Productivity paradox: reported gains 3x larger than implied revenue-based gains.

yale-restrepo-ai-automation-future-work-.title: Pascual Restrepo on AI, Automation, and the Future of Work
yale-restrepo-ai-automation-future-work-.publisher: Yale Department of Economics (Restrepo, interviewed by Strathmann)
yale-restrepo-ai-automation-future-work-.excerpt: A lot of these claims are premature. Many of the people making them have an interest in selling a product. Right now I would describe the labor market as more of a wait-and-see environment. You cannot automate everything tomorrow because we simply don't have enough computing power to do it.

brynjolfsson-hitzig-ai-knowledge-central.title: AI's Use of Knowledge in Society
brynjolfsson-hitzig-ai-knowledge-central.excerpt: The framework yields several predictions: larger average firm size, greater industry concentration, and reduced local managerial autonomy. Transformative AI sharply expands what counts as codifiable local knowledge. In the absence of active countermeasures, transformative AI may lead to significantly more centralization of decision-making.

deloitte-ai-state-enterprise-2026.title: State of AI in the Enterprise: The untapped edge
deloitte-ai-state-enterprise-2026.excerpt: Nearly 3 in 4 (74%) companies plan to deploy agentic AI within two years. 34% are already starting to use AI to deeply transform their businesses. 84% of companies have not redesigned jobs around AI capabilities.

marchesi-tang-ai-entrepreneurship-2025.title: When AI Meets Entrepreneurship: Evidence from the Commercialization of ChatGPT
marchesi-tang-ai-entrepreneurship-2025.excerpt: Industries more compatible with AI experienced an increase of over 10% in firm formation following ChatGPT's release. New firms are more likely to survive, grow faster, and attract more educated workers.

gupta-qian-simintzi-sun-genai-entreprene.title: Generative AI and Entrepreneurship
gupta-qian-simintzi-sun-genai-entreprene.excerpt: Exposed startups increased productivity, scaled faster, accelerated through financing rounds. VC shifted toward frequent, smaller investments, boosting new firm formation.

gofman-jin-ai-education-entrepreneurship.title: Artificial Intelligence, Education, and Entrepreneurship
gofman-jin-ai-education-entrepreneurship.excerpt: AI professors' startups raise $23M on average in less than 2 years; 20% are acquired within ~3.5 years. Documents AI professor brain drain from universities.

otis-clarke-genai-entrepreneurs-rct-2024.title: The Uneven Impact of Generative AI on Entrepreneurial Performance
otis-clarke-genai-entrepreneurs-rct-2024.publisher: Harvard Business School (Otis, Clarke, Delecourt, Holtz, Koning)

quickbooks-small-biz-ai-2025.title: Small Business AI Survey April 2025

census-bfs-baseline-2021.excerpt: New business applications hit record 5.4 million in 2021, a 24% increase over the 2019 pre-pandemic baseline.

fossen-sorgner-ai-self-employment-2024.title: Artificial Intelligence and Entrepreneurship
fossen-sorgner-ai-self-employment-2024.publisher: IZA / Foundations and Trends in Entrepreneurship (Fossen, McLemore, Sorgner)

a16z-bofa-solopreneur-2026.title: AI-Native Solopreneuring?

nber-hampole-ai-labor-2025.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Labor Market

nber-llm-small-effects-2025.title: Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects

nber-ai-productivity-unemployment-2025.title: AI, Productivity, and Technological Unemployment
nber-ai-productivity-unemployment-2025.excerpt: Calibrated to U.S. data, the model predicts more than threefold productivity improvements alongside a long-run employment loss of 23%, with half (~11.5%) occurring over the initial five-year transition period.

nber-firm-data-ai-2026.title: Firm Data on AI
nber-firm-data-ai-2026.excerpt: Synthesizes firm-level survey data from the US, UK, Germany, and Australia measuring AI's realized and expected impacts on sales per employee and employment. Data collected Feb-Apr 2025 and Nov 2025-Jan 2026.

dallasfed-young-workers-ai-2026.title: Young workers' employment drops in occupations with high AI exposure

mokyr-vickers-ziebarth-tech-anxiety-2015.title: The History of Technological Anxiety and the Future of Economic Growth: Is This Time Different?

autor-thompson-expertise-2025.title: Expertise
autor-thompson-expertise-2025.publisher: MIT / NBER (David Autor, Neil Thompson) — Schumpeter Lecture
autor-thompson-expertise-2025.excerpt: Resolves the long-standing puzzle of why routine task automation lowered employment but often raised wages in routine task-intensive occupations. Builds an 'expertise framework' on three pillars: hierarchical expertise, occupational task bundling, and automation. Key counterintuitive prediction: changes in occupational expertise requirements have OPPOSITE-signed effects on wages and employment — rising expertise raises wages but reduces the set of qualified workers (employment falls), falling expertise lowers wages but expands the eligible labor pool (employment rises). Empirically (303 harmonized Census occupations, 1980-2018): 0.1σ rise in occupational task expertise predicts a 5-7 log point fall in employment per decade, while a 10% expansion in task quantity predicts a 14% employment rise — opposite directions. Concrete case: Accounting clerks 1980-2018 saw employment fall 1.62M→1.11M (-31%) while wages rose $13.07→$18.17 (+39%); Stock/Inventory clerks saw employment rise 0.54M→1.48M (+175%) while wages fell $14.30→$12.43 (-13%). Routine task share fell 50.4%→32.2%; abstract share rose 33.2%→53.6%; 66% of removed tasks were routine, 77% of added tasks were abstract. Cross-occupation expertise wage premium nearly doubled: 1σ expertise = +16 log pts wages in 1980 vs. +31 log pts in 2018 (R² 0.32→0.49). Methodology: content-agnostic expertise measure via Efficient Coding Hypothesis on Standard Frequency Index; OpenAI text-embedding-3-small with 0.95 caliper to identify tasks removed/retained/added between 1977 DOT and 2018 O*NET.

lichtinger-hosseini-inequality-equalizer.title: AI Narrows Performance Gaps — But Does That Mean It Reduces Inequality?
lichtinger-hosseini-inequality-equalizer.excerpt: If AI dramatically boosts the productivity of high-paying knowledge work while leaving lower-paid service occupations largely unaffected, between-occupation inequality could widen even as within-task inequality narrows.

levanon-half-labor-force-2026.title: Half the Labor Force Is Having a Very Good Year

Within the same age band, young college graduates aged 22-34 sit at the 70th percentile of their own history since 2003 while young non-graduates sit at the 25th; the two series decoupled in 2024 after moving together for two decades.

tabarrok-firms-employment-2026.title: AI and Employment: So Far, So Good
tabarrok-firms-employment-2026.excerpt: Census has twice asked firms how AI use affected their total employment over the prior six months. In December 2023 to February 2024, when about 5% of firms used AI, "2.8% increased, 2.6% decreased and 94.6% reported no change." levanon-education-penalty-2026.title: The Education Penalty
levanon-education-penalty-2026.excerpt: In 2022, there was essentially no relationship between a metro area's share of college graduates and where its unemployment rate stood relative to its own history. The correlation was -0.01. Three years later, that correlation is 0.26 — modest but meaningful across more than 300 metropolitan areas.

fri-ai-economics-survey-2026.title: Forecasting the Economic Effects of AI
fri-ai-economics-survey-2026.publisher: Forecasting Research Institute (w/ Fed Chicago, Yale, Stanford, UPenn)
fri-ai-economics-survey-2026.excerpt: In a rapid AI progress scenario, economists forecast a drop in labor force participation from its 2025 baseline of 62.6% to 59.1% in 2030 and 55% in 2050, with roughly half of this decline—equivalent to 10 million jobs—attributable to AI.

nber-horton-coasean-agents-2026.title: The Coasean Singularity? Demand, Supply, and Market Design with AI Agents
nber-horton-coasean-agents-2026.excerpt: The activities that comprise transaction costs—learning prices, negotiating terms, writing contracts, and monitoring compliance—are precisely the types of tasks that AI agents can potentially perform at very low marginal cost. Once agents can indeed execute these functions effectively and cheaply, we will see significant shifts in the traditional make-or-buy boundaries that define firm organization and market structure.

kpmg-ai-pulse-q1-2026.title: AI Quarterly Pulse Survey Q1 2026
kpmg-ai-pulse-q1-2026.excerpt: 45% of leaders are willing to pay 11% to 15% more for strong AI skills

brookings-ai-career-pathways-2026.title: How AI may reshape career pathways to better jobs
brookings-ai-career-pathways-2026.publisher: Brookings Metro / Opportunity@Work (Heck, Muro, Methkupally, Siegmund)
brookings-ai-career-pathways-2026.excerpt: Of America's ~70M STARs (workers skilled through alternative routes, no four-year degree): 15.6M work in roles in the top quartile of AI exposure (43% of all top-quartile workers); 11M of those are in Gateway occupations — the stepping-stone roles connecting entry-level to higher-wage work — with 6 Gateway occupations alone accounting for ~8M of them. STARs are 62.3% of all Gateway-occupation workers. Across Destination occupations, 12.9M workers (~1/3) are highly exposed, including sales reps, accountants, financial managers. Only 51% of Gateway-to-Destination career pathways AVOID high AI exposure. 3.5M STARs are both highly exposed AND have low adaptive capacity (67% of all such workers). 23M STARs have low adaptive capacity overall (68% of all such workers). Highest pathway-exposure metros: Palm Bay FL (35.5%), Cape Coral FL (34.7%), Jacksonville (33%), Albany NY (32.8%), Harrisburg (32.6%), Providence (30.1%). 73% of US workers live and work in the same county, so disruption — and remediation — will be place-specific. stanford-del-enterprise-ai-playbook-2026.excerpt: Headcount reduction was the largest outcome in 45% of the deployments, but alternatives (hiring avoided, redeployment, no reduction) accounted for 55%. makela-stephany-complement-substitute-20.title: Complement or Substitute? How AI Increases the Demand for Human Skills

mit-futuretech-rising-tides-ai-automatio.title: Crashing Waves vs. Rising Tides: Preliminary Findings on AI Automation from Thousands of Worker Evaluations of Labor Market Tasks
mit-futuretech-rising-tides-ai-automatio.excerpt: AI models successfully complete tasks that take humans approximately 3-4 hours with about a 50% success rate, increasing to about 65% by 2025-Q3. nyfed-sce-ai-workplace-training-2026.title: Use of Gen AI in the Workplace and the Value of Access to Training

nyfed-sce-ai-workplace-training-2026.excerpt: Among currently employed respondents, 39 percent report that they are either using AI tools in their current job or have used AI tools in their jobs in the last twelve months. openai-jobs-transition-framework-2026.title: The AI Jobs Transition Framework: Mapping AI's Near-Term Impact on Jobs
openai-jobs-transition-framework-2026.excerpt: All 921 occupations (147.9M jobs) sort into four categories: 18% are at a higher short-term automation risk, 46% are less likely to experience near-term change, 12% could grow because of AI, and 24% may see declining employment as their task composition shifts but remaining jobs will still need workers. ChatGPT is used about 3x more in the kinds of jobs our framework identifies as most at risk of automation. Capability overhang by archetype: high-automation-risk jobs show 23.8% realized vs 90.0% theoretical exposure (66.2pp gap); jobs that grow with AI 22.7% vs 72.4% (49.7pp); reorganize 14.9% vs 67.1% (52.3pp); less immediate change 6.4% vs 27.4% (21.0pp). nber-chen-sialm-xu-ai-investing-2026.publisher: NBER (Shuang Chen, Clemens Sialm, David X. Xu)
nber-chen-sialm-xu-ai-investing-2026.excerpt: AI-driven investing has grown steadily since the early 2010s and is concentrated among hedge funds. Average AI labor intensity is 1.17% of job postings at SEC-registered investment advisers. AI hedge funds peaked at ~2.7% of all hedge funds in 2023.

jacobs-canedy-wioa-retraining-2026.title: Did US Worker Retraining Reduce Participant Automation Exposure?
jacobs-canedy-wioa-retraining-2026.publisher: arXiv (Julian Jacobs, Oxford/DeepMind; Jordan Canedy, FRI)
jacobs-canedy-wioa-retraining-2026.excerpt: WIOA rarely supports worker resilience to automation, with 45% of all WIOA participants returning to their prior industry of work, and 27% staying in the same occupation. Successful outcomes driven mostly by wage gains, possibly due to catch-up mean reversion, rather than changes in occupation.

nyt-schneider-ai-augmentation-2026.title: A.I. Doesn't Have to Mean Layoffs
nyt-schneider-ai-augmentation-2026.excerpt: In the last three months of 2025, call centers fielded 150,000 questions. Three-quarters of the time, A.I. was able to provide the right answer to straightforward questions. The agent then reviews and if necessary, modifies and refines the answer with the caller.
